stem:
A 6-month-old with bronchiolitis has SpO₂ of 88% on room air.

What is the target oxygen saturation?

options.label: A
options.explanation: >88% is too low — this would accept significant hypoxaemia. Guidelines recommend ≥90%.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Correct — target SpO₂ ≥90% in bronchiolitis, per the BIDS trial showing equivalence of a 90% target to a 94% target. Supplemental O₂ (nasal prongs, high-flow) is indicated if SpO₂ <90%. This infant at 88% needs oxygen therapy immediately.

options.label: C
options.explanation: >98% is unrealistic and unnecessary — normal infant SpO₂ in sleep can dip to 92-94%.

options.label: D
options.explanation: >95% is unnecessarily high — attempting to maintain >95% may prolong oxygen therapy and hospital stay without clinical benefit.

context:
Target SpO₂ in bronchiolitis is at or above 90% on room air or supplemental oxygen — the BIDS trial (Cunningham et al., Lancet 2015) validated a 90% target as non-inferior to a 94% target, supporting adoption of the lower threshold.

Chasing higher saturations (94-98%) prolongs admissions, increases parental anxiety, and exposes infants to unnecessary oxygen without improving recovery.
